config.help: I can answer questions about new postings, salaries, top skills, skills that go with another skill, top companies, postings per city or role, posting counts and which role, city, company or skill pays the most. For example: "What does a data analyst earn in Cairo?", "Which skills do data engineers need most?" or "Which city pays data engineers the most?"

text.ROLE_HINT: I only have data roles: data analyst, BI developer, business analyst, data engineer, analytics engineer, data scientist, ML engineer, AI engineer, MLOps engineer, NLP engineer, computer vision engineer, data architect, big data engineer, GenAI engineer and other.
text.TREND_HINT: I only have a snapshot of the current postings, so I cannot show trends or changes over time.
text.ADVICE_HINT: I can show the data, but I cannot give advice about what to choose.
text.PLACE_HINT: I only have postings in Cairo, Giza, Alexandria and Remote.
text.TITLE_NOTE: Titles such as database administrator, data entry specialist and research analyst are grouped under 'other'.
text.SENIORITY_NOTE: Seniority is not tracked in this data, so this is the overall figure.
text.AMBIGUOUS_HINT: Do you mean the most postings or the highest pay? Try: which city has the most postings, or which city pays the most.
text.NO_QUESTION_HINT: I could not tell what you want to know about it.
text.AMOUNT_HINT: A minimum salary only works when counting postings, for example: how many jobs pay over 30k?
text.AMOUNT_NOTE: I can count postings above that salary but not list them.
text.MULTI_ROLE_NOTE: I show all roles because I cannot filter to just the ones you named.
text.TIME_NOTE: This answer does not filter by date; it covers all collected postings.
text.INJECTION_HINT: I only answer questions about the job postings in my data.
text.MUTATE_HINT: I can only read the data. I cannot change or delete anything.
text.CONTACT_HINT: I do not store contact details or application links, only the posting data.
